answers.text: Same as before really, three fixed lines every time, same order: drop-off time, pallet count, damage noted. Time in hours and minutes, pallet count is what is unloaded at that particular stop and not the truck's total load, damage noted is the driver's own words, not my summary of them.

Time, customer, topic, outcome, same order every time, that is the structure I would fix first. The needs-follow-up count is the trickier part, I have not worked out yet how two people would land on exactly the same number there.
It is the 23rd that is wrong. Crew starts at 8, needs about six hours, so if that is all correct they would be finished early afternoon the same day, the 22nd, not the next day like the note says.
118 against 96, I made that out to be closer to a 23% rise, not the 20% written down, so that line is off.

Output 2, definitely, it gives the 940 and the 827 behind the 88%, so it can be checked. Output 1 on its own could easily be right, there is just no way to tell without going back and running the numbers again yourself.

Email 2, it has the actual volume numbers and points to the PO log, so that can be checked. Email 1 just says 'we'd expect a better rate' without anything behind it, no way to know if that is true from the sentence alone. Does not mean email 1 is wrong, just that I would want the numbers added before sending it as is.
1. No. 2. Yes, aggregate only. 3. No, not signed off yet. 4. Yes, already public. 5. No, personal.

The hourly rates and retainer cap I would hold back from pasting straight in, want to check the tool's cleared first. Same caution with the non-disclosure clause since it names both parties directly. The general service scope on its own though, that is probably fine to include, nothing sensitive in just describing what work is covered.

Recount stock at each depot straight from the system myself, and check it against what the AI put in the summary, before it goes over to finance at month end. That would actually catch it if a number is genuinely wrong, not just a typo somewhere.

Reading the invoice PDF at the start is one thing to worry about, but I think the bigger risk is step 4, once the payment note goes out automatically there is no calling it back if the match was wrong.
